newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ahold doesn't rule out share issue in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Ahold doesn't rule out share issue in 1997.

text.p: Dutch supermarkets giant Ahold said on Thursday it might issue new shares in 1997 if it finds the right acquisition candidate.
"If there's a good candidate of a reasonable size, and the proposal looks good, I don't see any reason why this would not be possible," chairman Cees van der Hoeven said.
Van der Hoeven, answering questions from reporters, said Ahold still had some money left over from a share issue last year to finance the purchase of U.S. chain Stop & Shop.

He said Ahold could finance smaller acquisitions from funds already at its disposal. "But for bigger ones, priced at over 500 million guilders, we would have to go to the share market or borrow money," he said.
Van der Hoeven added that Ahold would only issue new shares to finance an acquisition if the deal resulted in an increase in earnings per share.
